neutral_facts.value: The accused, an army personnel, was on security duty with two other sentries. An incident of stone throwing occurred, and a Quick Reaction Team was summoned. The accused chased a member of the Quick Reaction Team, who was warned not to fire. Despite the warning, the accused fired three shots from a distance of 8 to 10 feet, killing the victim. The weapon used matched the one issued to the accused, and the cartridge cases found at the scene were consistent with the weapon. The accused was apprehended and stated that he did what he had to do.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the killing was a deliberate act of murder, as the accused fired three shots at a member of the Quick Reaction Team despite being warned, and the evidence supported the findings of the Court Martial.

quotes.text: The Court Martial ... held that the shooting was a deliberate attack of murder and the appellant was accordingly guilty under Section 302 of the IPC.
It is also apparent from the evidence of PW.14 that he had cautioned the appellant ... but despite this warning the appellant fired three shots.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the killing was an accident arising from a suspicion of a terrorist attack and that a case under Section 302 of the IPC was not made out.

quotes.text: Mr. D. Thakur, the learned counsel for the appellant, has pointed out that from the facts of the case it was apparent that the killing was an accident and arose from a suspicion of a terrorist attack
He accordingly prays that a case under Section 302 was not made out.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that courts should not interfere with the findings of fact recorded by the Court Martial unless there is a clear error, and that the evidence must be considered as a whole.

quotes.text: The Court would not, in these circumstances, interfere with the same.
This Court would not, in these circumstances, interfere in the assessment.

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence was imposed because the Court Martial found the shooting to be a deliberate act of murder, and the High Court upheld these findings, so the Supreme Court did not interfere with the sentencing.
